handbookNote: Minnesota Department of Natural Resources (DNR) boat and water safety program (dnr.state.mn.us) -- Minnesota has no single official state-administered boating knowledge exam; boaters satisfy the state's mandatory boater education law (Minn. Stat. 86B.302, 86B.304) by completing a DNR-approved water safety course and its embedded written test, by presenting proof of an accepted reciprocal program, or by completing a commissioner-certified equivalent program, with most students completing the requirement through a delegated third-party provider's own online course and exam (e.g., Boat-ed.com, an authorized DNR provider) rather than a state-run exam -- the mandate itself is a genuine, currently phasing-in law confirmed independently by two sources (the Minnesota DNR's own boater-education-law page and Boat-ed.com's Minnesota course page): a watercraft operator's permit is required on a birth-date phase-in schedule -- born after June 30, 2004 (required starting July 1, 2025), born after June 30, 2000 (July 1, 2026), born after June 30, 1996 (July 1, 2027), and born after June 30, 1987 (July 1, 2028) -- with those born before July 1, 1987 generally exempt unless renting a vessel or serving as a required accompanying operator; minimum unsupervised operating age is 12, a child under 12 may operate a motorboat under 75 HP only with an accompanying operator aboard and may never operate a PWC regardless of supervision, motors rated 25 HP or less are excluded from the permit requirement entirely, and statutory exemptions cover USCG license holders, Canadian Pleasure Craft Operator Card holders, nonresidents present under 60 days, licensed dealers, and emergency operators -- the exact final-exam question count/passing percentage is not uniformly published across Minnesota's DNR-authorized course vendors and is therefore left unconfirmed rather than asserted as a specific number -- content is also grounded in real Minnesota statute detail verified directly against the Minnesota Revisor of Statutes (revisor.mn.gov): personal watercraft-specific rules under Minn. Stat. 86B.313 (150-foot slow-no-wake distance from shorelines/docks/swimmers/other watercraft, an operating-hours ban from one hour before sunset to 9:30 a.m., mandatory PFDs for riders and towed persons, a towing observer-or-mirror requirement, engine cutoff lanyard requirement, wildlife-harassment prohibition, and dealer disclosure duties), PFD/child life jacket requirements under Sec. 86B.501 (children under 10 must wear a PFD unless below deck or in an enclosed cabin), fire extinguisher and fuel ventilation requirements under Sec. 86B.531, navigation lights (Sec. 86B.511) and capacity plates (Sec. 86B.505), Sophia's Law carbon monoxide detector and warning-sticker requirements for motorboats with enclosed accommodation spaces under Sec. 86B.532, boating-while-impaired law under Sec. 86B.33 (incorporating the 0.08 alcohol concentration standard from Chapter 169A, owner liability for knowingly permitting an intoxicated operator, and ignition interlock program cross-application), post-accident duties to stop/render aid/exchange information and report to the county sheriff under Sec. 86B.341, coroner reporting and mandatory toxicology testing for certain watercraft fatalities under Sec. 86B.335, vessel registration (Sec. 86B.401, 3-year registration cycle) and titling for boats over 16 feet (Sec. 86B.825, 86B.830), and Minnesota's aquatic invasive species law (Minn. Stat. 84D.10) requiring drain plugs, bailers, and valves to be removed or opened before transporting watercraft away from any water access, with conservation officer authority to order decontamination or bar relaunch until corrected -- plus universal NASBLA-aligned boating-safety fundamentals (Navigation Rules, Uniform State Waterway Marking System aids to navigation, PFD types, required equipment, cold-water immersion/HELP position, weather, and towed water sports) applied to Minnesota's roughly 10,000+ lake recreational boating culture, including DNR conservation officer statewide enforcement authority and the DNR's 'Own Your Wake' responsible-wake-boating program -- price matches this project's Motorcycle-tier boating convention ($7.99), not a placeholder
